note: What an account needs before it can be opened, funded and traded. Onboarding stalls on absence far more than on difficulty, so this is the list a mandate is checked against. Items marked external can never be satisfied by reading the document — they are operational artifacts that must be chased separately, and naming them as such is the point.

blocking_levels.funding: Account cannot be funded until this is resolved
blocking_levels.trading: Account can be funded but must not trade until this is resolved
blocking_levels.billing: Does not block trading. Blocks the first invoice
blocking_levels.reporting: Does not block trading. Blocks the first client report

items.label: Governing law and jurisdiction stated
items.note: Drives which regulatory regime the account sits under.

items.label: Executed IMA on file
items.note: A guidelines exhibit is not evidence the agreement was executed.

items.label: Legal entity name and LEI captured
items.note: Required for reporting and counterparty setup. Rarely in the guidelines document.

items.label: Authorised signers and trading authority confirmed
Benchmark named
items.note: Benchmark-relative restrictions cannot be coded or monitored without it.

items.label: Vehicle and structure confirmed
items.note: Separate account, commingled fund or sub-advised. Drives most downstream setup.

items.label: Funding date and initial funding method agreed
items.note: Cash or in-kind. In-kind funding pulls in transition management and a legacy asset review.

items.label: Every restriction coded with no unresolved ambiguity
items.note: The single most common reason an account is funded but cannot trade.

items.label: Restricted list file delivered and feed established
items.note: The rule is codeable from the document. The list never is — it is a recurring data feed with its own delivery mechanism and update cadence.

items.label: ESG data vendor named for revenue-threshold screens
items.note: Vendors classify differently. A screen without a named vendor is not implementable, it only looks like it is.

items.label: Tracking error measurement basis specified
items.note: Ex ante and ex post produce different breach profiles from the same portfolio.

items.label: Rating floor test point and downgrade treatment specified
items.note: At purchase versus ongoing is the difference between a clean book and a permanent breach queue.

items.label: Rules loaded into the compliance engine and tested against a model portfolio
Standing settlement instructions established
items.note: A named custodian is not the same as working SSIs. New custodians take the longest.

items.label: Trade instruction method and cutoff agreed
Counterparty and broker accounts opened
items.note: Derivatives usage implies ISDA and CSA negotiation, which runs on a legal timeline, not an ops one.

items.label: Cash sweep and income handling instruction on file
Billing frequency and arrears or advance basis stated
Billing contact and invoice delivery method confirmed
Composite assignment agreed
items.note: GIPS requires assignment prospectively. Retrofitting an account into a composite after the fact is a problem.

items.label: Report recipients and delivery channel confirmed
items.note: The document says what to send and when. It almost never says to whom or how.
